groups.name: Citrus terpenic
groups.role: Opening lift, bitter peel, twig, and high-frequency contrast.
groups.risks: Cleaner, terpene harshness, short-lived opening, oxidation.

groups.name: Aldehydic
groups.role: Lift, abstraction, cold shimmer, wax, air, and masking.
groups.risks: Soap, wax, detergent, harsh trigeminal edge.

groups.name: Aromatic herbs and lavender
groups.role: Aromatic identity, freshness, masculine structure, and top-heart continuity.
groups.risks: Soap, medicinal dryness, fougere cliché.

groups.name: Spices
groups.role: Contrast, temperature, kinetic lift, and aromatic bridging.
groups.risks: Toothpaste, culinary literalness, medicinal sharpness.

groups.name: Violet ionones
groups.role: Violet petal, berry shadow, woody mobility, and cosmetic/powder spectrum.
groups.risks: Candy, lipstick, anosmia dependence, woody abstraction.

groups.name: Orris irones and rhizome
groups.role: Waxy orris, wet root, dry rhizome, luxury depth, and violet-root continuity.
groups.risks: Salty carrot, lipstick powder, green iris, root mud.

groups.name: Rose floral
groups.role: Petal body, rosy brightness, metallic lift, and fruit-floral depth.
groups.risks: Soap, jam, metallic rose, cosmetic bouquet.

groups.name: Jasmine and white floral
groups.role: Living floral bloom, petal volume, indolic depth, and floral air.
groups.risks: Banana, grape, mothball, bubblegum, floral blur.

groups.name: Muguet, magnolia, and floral air
groups.role: Clean petal volume, muguet softness, watery bloom, and negative space.
groups.risks: Detergent, shampoo, identity dilution, generic floral air.

groups.name: Green leaf and stem
groups.role: Living leaf, wet stem, naturalism, bitterness, and green contrast.
groups.risks: Cucumber, lawn clippings, swamp, harsh galbanum.

groups.name: Marine, ozonic, and mineral
groups.role: Air, dew, mineral space, water, and cool diffusion.
groups.risks: Aquatic detergent, melon, blue fragrance genericity.

groups.name: Fruit esters, apple, and pear
groups.role: Juice, peel, green fruit, sparkling top, and fruit-floral motion.
groups.risks: Shampoo, pineapple candy, pear/apple confusion.

groups.name: Lactones, stone fruit, and osmanthus
groups.role: Peach/apricot flesh, creamy fruit, osmanthus leather, and soft volume.
groups.risks: Coconut, peach candy, lipstick cream, apricot jam.

groups.name: Honey, tobacco, cocoa, coffee, and nuts
groups.role: Honeyed warmth, roasted depth, tobacco leaf, cocoa, and nut texture.
groups.risks: Maple syrup, burnt popcorn, ashtray, edible overload.

groups.name: Vanilla, tonka, heliotrope, and powder
groups.role: Powder, almond, tonka, vanilla warmth, and soft rounding.
groups.risks: Frosting, pastille, lipstick, candle, syrup.

groups.name: Cedar, vetiver, patchouli, and root woods
groups.role: Grain, root, dryness, earth, structure, and natural wood complexity.
groups.risks: Pencil shavings, root mud, camphor, smoke.

groups.name: Sandalwood and creamy woods
groups.role: Cream, polish, dark wood, radiant sandalwood, and tactile fibers.
groups.risks: One-molecule sandalwood, buttery takeover, synthetic monolith.

groups.name: Transparent woods
groups.role: Spatial volume, transparent grain, diffusion, textile warmth, and bridging.
groups.risks: Abstract wood cloud, formula homogenization, dry emptiness.

groups.name: Ambergris and amberwoods
groups.role: Mineral persistence, projection, dry pressure, and late skeleton.
groups.risks: Scratch, woody-amber wall, anosmia/fatigue, drydown collapse.

groups.name: Macrocyclic and clean musks
groups.role: Skin diffusion, radiance, softness, metallic cleanliness, and persistence.
groups.risks: Specific anosmia, laundry, fruity musk shampoo, loss of detail.

groups.name: Polycyclic, nitro, and powdery musks
groups.role: Soft volume, powder, warmth, and long diffuse body.
groups.risks: Laundry fog, powder, sweetness, flattened contrast.

groups.name: Resins, incense, benzoin, and moss
groups.role: Incense, balsam, moss, amber warmth, smoke, and slow evolution.
groups.risks: Sticky balsam, candle, medicinal smoke, floral suppression.

groups.name: Suede, leather, smoke, and animalic
groups.role: Tactile suede, animalic warmth, saffron leather, smoke, and dark shadow.
groups.risks: Burnt rubber, barnyard, hospital bandage, handbag leather.

interactions.a_effect_on_b: Citrus supplies recognizable peel and terpene body beneath aldehydic sparkle.
interactions.b_effect_on_a: Aldehydes increase apparent brightness, abstraction, and reach of citrus.
interactions.dose_window: Aldehydes at trace-to-low relative to citrus
interactions.phase_window: opening
interactions.failure_mode: Cleaner, wax, or harshness; the aldehyde can erase peel identity.
interactions.physical_test: Compare citrus alone against 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1% aldehydic-module additions at equal total loading.

interactions.a_effect_on_b: Citrus lightens herbs and keeps lavender from reading soapy or heavy.
interactions.b_effect_on_a: Aromatics extend citrus into the heart and add natural twig/herb continuity.
interactions.dose_window: Citrus usually larger than aromatic herbs in the opening
interactions.phase_window: opening to heart
interactions.failure_mode: Cologne cliché, soap, or bitter petitgrain overload.
interactions.physical_test: Test 3:1, 1:1, and 1:3 citrus:aromatic modules through 2 hours.

interactions.a_effect_on_b: Citrus makes cardamom/coriander feel brighter and less culinary.
interactions.b_effect_on_a: Spice gives citrus temperature, persistence, and masculine tension.
interactions.dose_window: Spice usually trace-to-moderate against the citrus block
interactions.phase_window: opening to heart
interactions.failure_mode: Gin, toothpaste, culinary peel, or black-pepper harshness.
interactions.physical_test: Evaluate coriander, cardamom, and pepper separately against the same citrus base.

MIX_SUPPRESSION.title: Odour mixture suppression: evidence for a peripheral mechanism in human and rat
MIX_SUPPRESSION.use: Mixture components can suppress each other; relative intensity and chemistry matter.

OR_MIXTURE_MODULATION.title: Modulation of the combinatorial code of odorant receptor response patterns in odorant mixtures
OR_MIXTURE_MODULATION.use: Odorants can produce additive, suppressive, antagonistic, and inverse-agonist effects at receptors.

CONFIGURAL_MIXTURE.title: Configural perception of a binary olfactory mixture
CONFIGURAL_MIXTURE.use: Some mixtures generate a new odor object rather than a simple sum of components.

SELECTIVE_ADAPTATION.title: Characteristic component odors emerge from mixtures after selective adaptation
SELECTIVE_ADAPTATION.use: Dominant components may mask others; adaptation can unmask concealed qualities.

CROSS_ADAPTATION.title: A comparison of self-adaptation and cross-adaptation to odorants presented singly and in mixtures
CROSS_ADAPTATION.use: Adaptation is substantially odor-specific, supporting repeated-day and temporal testing.

RECEPTOR_COMPETITION.title: Neural coding of binary mixtures in a structurally related odorant pair
RECEPTOR_COMPETITION.use: Structurally related odorants often show hypoadditivity through receptor competition.

NASAL_METABOLISM.title: Nasal Odorant Competitive Metabolism Is Involved in the Human Olfactory Process
NASAL_METABOLISM.use: Odorants can alter one another's nasal metabolism and apparent availability.

TRIGEMINAL_MODULATION.title: Neuropeptide receptors provide a signalling pathway for trigeminal modulation of olfactory transduction
TRIGEMINAL_MODULATION.use: Irritant/trigeminal stimulation can attenuate and distort odor response.

ALDEHYDE_MASKING.title: Application of the Olfactoscan method to study masking by saturated aldehydes
ALDEHYDE_MASKING.use: Masking can be highly odorant-specific rather than a generic intensity effect.

FRAGRANCE_EVAPORATION.title: An innovative device for in vivo and in vitro study of fragrance evaporation
FRAGRANCE_EVAPORATION.use: Release depends on surface, time, matrix, temperature, and physicochemical properties.

RESIDUAL_SKIN.title: Assessing residual fragrances on skin after body washing
RESIDUAL_SKIN.use: Sampling method and fiber alter recovered headspace; substantive materials can persist for many hours.

BODY_ODOR_PERFUME.title: Psychology of fragrance use: individual odor and perfume blends
BODY_ODOR_PERFUME.use: Perfume interacts with the wearer's own odor rather than merely masking it.

HEDIONE_VARIATION.title: Prior exposure to Hedione does not affect attractiveness ratings
HEDIONE_VARIATION.use: Substantial individual sensitivity variation to Hedione cautions against making it the only floral-air mechanism.

MUSK_OR5A2.title: An odorant receptor that senses four classes of musk compounds
MUSK_OR5A2.use: Different musk structural classes can converge perceptually while remaining receptor-distinct.

MUSK_RECEPTOR_TRILOGY.title: The trilogy of human musk receptors
MUSK_RECEPTOR_TRILOGY.use: Genetic variants can shift musk thresholds by tens-fold; mixed musk systems reduce reliance on one receptor path.

MUSK_MECHANISM.title: Molecular mechanism of human musk receptors OR5AN1 and OR1A1
MUSK_MECHANISM.use: Musk classes differ in receptor activity and stereochemical response.

HUMAN_OR_HELIONAL.title: Specificity and sensitivity of a human olfactory receptor
HUMAN_OR_HELIONAL.use: Helional activates a specific human receptor, supporting careful watery-floral dosing and interaction testing.

SPECIFIC_ANOSMIA_SALICYLATE.title: Decreasing prevalence of specific anosmia to non-steroid odorants
SPECIFIC_ANOSMIA_SALICYLATE.use: Sensitivity to methyl salicylate and other odorants varies by individual and development.

SPECIFIC_ANOSMIA_PLASTICITY.title: Investigating plasticity of the olfactory system through specific anosmia
SPECIFIC_ANOSMIA_PLASTICITY.use: Specific anosmia can affect benzyl salicylate, bacdanol, maltol, and other perfumery materials.

SANDALWOOD_SAR_1.title: Syntheses and odor of bulky-group-modified sandalwood odorants
SANDALWOOD_SAR_1.use: Small structural changes can move sandalwood odor toward generic wood.

SANDALWOOD_COMPOSITION.title: Comparison of selected commercial sandalwood oils
SANDALWOOD_COMPOSITION.use: Natural sandalwood, Amyris, and synthetic sandalwood systems are compositionally distinct.

PEACH_LACTONE_IONONE.title: Volatile and odorous compounds in peach varieties
PEACH_LACTONE_IONONE.use: Lactones, beta-ionone, esters, and aldehydes jointly contribute to stone-fruit odor.

METHYL_SALICYLATE_FLORAL.title: Floral scent emission of Epiphyllum oxypetalum
METHYL_SALICYLATE_FLORAL.use: Methyl salicylate can be a real floral-emission component, but its dosage and context are species-dependent.

IRONE_PATENT.title: Irone-rich perfume compositions
IRONE_PATENT.use: Supports irone function in orris/violet architecture, not a commercial formula claim.

MUGUET_PATENT.title: Modern muguet fragrance compositions
MUGUET_PATENT.use: Supports multi-material muguet construction and replacement logic.

WHITE_PETAL_PATENT.title: White-petal perfume oil example
WHITE_PETAL_PATENT.use: Shows distributed floral, musk, salicylate, aldehydic, and diffusion architecture.
